report.summary: Imports module: all-language import extraction and internal resolution, with tree-sitter and regex fallback.
risks: extract_imports | medium | Returns [] for Python, but claim says Python handled by parse.python_imports; uncheckable if that exists. | Check that parse.python_imports is implemented and called appropriately.
_candidate_paths for Rust | medium | 'use crate::foo::Bar' (Bar is in foo.rs) logic adds parent.rs; may produce false positives for multi-level paths. | Verify with real Rust code patterns.
_candidate_paths for Java/Kotlin | medium | Static member import logic may produce incorrect candidate if no '/' in base. | Test with static import like 'import a.b.C.m'.
_match_file | low | Prefers shallowest match; may not always be correct for deep directory structures. | Consider if deeper match should be preferred in some cases.
resolve_internal | low | Best-effort; unresolved edges dropped silently. | Ensure this is acceptable behavior for the system.

handoff.purpose: All-language import extraction and internal resolution.

symbols.name: _CANDIDATE_LANGS
symbols.note: Set of languages whose imports are treated as internal candidates.

symbols.name: _JS_EXTS
symbols.note: Tuple of JavaScript/TypeScript file extensions for resolution.

symbols.name: extract_imports
symbols.note: Extracts imports from non-Python files using tree-sitter or regex fallback.

symbols.name: _ts_import_nodes
symbols.note: Extracts import node texts using tree-sitter AST.

symbols.name: _REGEX_FALLBACK
symbols.note: Dictionary of compiled regex patterns per language for fallback import extraction.

symbols.name: _regex_import_nodes
symbols.note: Extracts import lines using regex fallback patterns.

symbols.name: _parse_import
symbols.note: Parses a single import node text into (raw, kind) pairs per language.

symbols.name: resolve_internal
symbols.note: Maps an internal import raw string to a repo file path, best-effort.

symbols.name: _candidate_paths
symbols.note: Generates ordered candidate file paths for import resolution per language.

symbols.name: _candidate_dirs
symbols.note: Generates candidate directory segments for package/dir-style imports (Go, QML).

symbols.name: _match_file
symbols.note: Matches a candidate path against known files, preferring shallowest match.

claims.text: Python keeps its precise ``parse.python_imports`` path (relative-import resolution intact); THIS module handles every OTHER language
claims.why: The claim refers to parse.python_imports which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: With tree-sitter installed it walks the grammar's ``import_types`` nodes (precise node boundaries); without it, a per-language regex fallback keeps the edges flowing at lower precision.
claims.why: Code shows _ts_import_nodes uses spec.import_types and _regex_import_nodes as fallback.

claims.text: Each edge is ``(raw, kind)`` where ``kind`` is 'internal' (a resolution candidate — a repo-local module) or 'external' (a library / stdlib import).
claims.why: extract_imports returns list of (raw, kind) and _parse_import assigns 'internal' or 'external'.

claims.text: ``resolve_internal`` — map an internal ``raw`` to an actual repo file by path/suffix match against the known file set.
claims.why: resolve_internal function does exactly that using known, by_basename, by_dir_tail.

claims.text: This is **best-effort** for non-Python languages: module->file conventions (Rust ``mod.rs``, Java source roots, Go packages-as-directories, C++ inline namespaces) are only approximated without a real build graph.
claims.why: Code shows approximations: Rust mod.rs, Java .java, Go dirs, C++ include patterns.

claims.text: Unresolved edges are simply dropped (no false edge), never guessed.
claims.why: resolve_internal returns None if no match, and caller presumably drops it.

claims.text: The ``kind`` distinction is syntactic where a language marks it (C ``"x"`` vs ``<x>``, Rust ``crate::``/``self::``/``super::``, JS relative ``./x``, QML quoted dir imports); for the dotted-name languages that give NO syntactic internal/external signal (Java, Kotlin, C#, PHP, Go) every import is treated as an internal *candidate* and the file-set match is the real arbiter.
claims.why: Code: C uses quote vs angle, Rust checks first token, JS checks start with ./ or /, QML checks quotes; Java etc. always return 'internal' in _parse_import.

claims.text: Python returns [] — it is resolved precisely by ``parse.python_imports`` in ``index.py``.
claims.why: References parse.python_imports and index.py not in this chunk.

claims.text: Iterative pre-order walk. A recursive one blows Python's recursion limit on deeply nested real-world ASTs (long chained/generated expressions) — push children reversed so they pop back in source order.
claims.why: Code uses a stack, pushes children reversed, pops to traverse.

claims.text: Per-language fallback line patterns (no tree-sitter). Best-effort by design.
claims.why: _REGEX_FALLBACK dictionary exists with patterns for each language.

claims.text: module specifier is the last string literal
claims.why: Code: spec_path = strings[-1] takes the last string.
Code: path = re.split(r"::\s*[{*]", body, 1)[0].strip() removes group/glob.
Code: body.rstrip('.*').rstrip('.') removes trailing .* and dot.
Code: re.sub(r'^\w+\s*=\s*', '', body) removes alias prefix.

claims.text: Match is by suffix / directory containment; the first, most specific hit wins.
claims.why: Code iterates candidate_paths then candidate_dirs, returns first hit.

claims.text: prefer the shallowest (closest to root) match
claims.why: Code: if best is None or len(rel) < len(best): best = rel chooses shorter path.

observations.what: extract_imports returns [] for Python, but relies on external parse.python_imports which is not present in this chunk.
Rust candidate path generation adds parent.rs for 'use crate::foo::Bar' which may be incorrect for multi-level paths like 'use crate::foo::bar::Baz'.
Java/Kotlin static member import handling may produce incorrect candidate if base has no '/' (e.g., 'import C.m' -> candidate 'C.java' and then 'C.java' again).
_match_file prefers shallowest match by path length; this may not always be correct (e.g., deeper match might be intended).
resolve_internal silently drops unresolved edges; no logging or error indication.
